decisions.note: Round 4 presentation (open/edit/dedupe) never surfaced any delete capability; client explicitly asked 'how do I get rid of one?' — caught pre-implementation, at prototype stage.
Round 4 editor let the client fix title/summary but not the url itself; client asked to also fix 'the actual web address' — caught at prototype stage.

Round 5's delete-with-undo made client realize 'not everything should be gone forever'; she named a distinct reversible tuck-away state the maker hadn't offered — caught at prototype stage, before archive was ever built.

Round 6 modeled 'read later' as a plain topic tag; client rejected this and specified the reference-correct shape (a distinct status with its own view and a check-off-to-clear action), which the maker then built in round 7.
Round 9's link-rot handling only preserved title+summary; client pushed for the reference behavior of actually preserving the page content itself, supplied in round 10 as the full local snapshot.

Round 12 introduced bare-word 'or'/'not' operators without the reference's quoting escape for literal operator words; client flagged the gap ('what if the word I want IS or') and the quote-escape rule (REF-BM-15) was added in round 13.

Through round 12 tag-filter and full-text search worked only as separate, un-combined features; client asked whether search could be scoped to a label/pile, and this composition was built in round 14.

Round 14 stepping-back review: client asked for saving a search+label combination for reuse, a bundle feature never surfaced by the maker — caught at spec-gate/step-back stage, left for a future round.
Round 14 review: client asked to bring in existing browser bookmarks and get data back out, an import/export capability never surfaced up to that point — caught at the same step-back gate.
Round 14 review: client asked for choosing list order (newest-first, by name) which had never been offered — caught at step-back gate, deferred to next round.
Round 14 review: client asked for multi-select bulk actions (batch archive/label), never surfaced — caught at step-back gate, deferred to next round.

Once export was actually built (round 16 on), it produced a proprietary JSON backup file rather than the reference's Netscape HTML export format; client only ever verified functional round-trip completeness, never the format — a satisficing miss.

After the packaging saga failed (rounds 19-23), Path A (round 24-28) dropped automatic title/description/favicon/image capture for newly-pasted links entirely; client consciously accepted this trade-off rather than pushing back at runtime — an accepted, uncaught divergence from REF-BM-02.

Path A (round 24-28) also dropped local snapshot preservation and dead-link content entirely; client named it 'the big casualty' but affirmed the reduced build rather than blocking acceptance on it — a knowingly accepted, uncaught divergence, logged only as a future wish.
